question.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{3-4y{x}^{3}}{y}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}(\frac{3}{y}-4{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}\frac{3}{y}\text{ }\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}4{x}^{3}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{3}{y}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(2-1){\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{3}{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[3\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|]_{1}^{e} \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}4{x}^{3}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(e-1){\int }_{1}^{2}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(e-1)[{x}^{4}]_{1}^{2} \\  & =(e-1)({2}^{4}-{1}^{4}) \\  & =15(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{3-4y{x}^{3}}{y}\,\text{d}A=3-15(e-1)=18-15e.\end{aligned}
$$
